records.habit: Fast-growing arching woody shrub or small tree, horticultural 5–15 ft tall, long slender stems
records.leaves: Opposite, ovate–elliptic, 4–9 × 1.5–6 cm; margins dentate, variable pubescence, green above and often paler beneath
records.inflorescence: Lax, often flexuose axillary racemes, sometimes several per leaf axil; flowers small, white, strongly fragrant
records.habitat: Native South American lowland scrub and disturbed habitats, not Texas-native
records.phenology: July through frost in horticultural NC reference; not a universal native-range season
records.taxon_note: Kew notes great variability in tooth pattern, size, and hairiness of leaves; avoid over-specific field key.

records.habit: Perennial shrub; drooping stems to around five feet long in Wildflower Center treatment for subsp. racemosa
records.flowers: White to yellow (subsp. racemosa Wildflower Center profile)
records.habitat: Dry, shaded habitat in Wildflower Center profile; Kew reports native range Texas Edwards Plateau
records.taxon_note: Source subspecies racemosa only; species level can include other infraspecific taxa. Leaves and quantitative corolla characters held for primary FNA treatment.

records.habit: Aromatic low, basally much-branched plant, arching stems to approximately 10 in (25 cm) in southwestern field account
records.leaves: Small ovate to roundish leaves ca. 1/3 inch (8 mm) long, entire and often with pointed tips
records.flowers: Whorls above leafy lower stems; purple calyx with upper 3 lobes partly fused and lower two free; pink-purple two-lipped corolla with white patch on lower lip
records.habitat: Rocky canyons and limestone outcrops; field account describes 3,000–6,500 ft elevations in Southwest
records.taxon_note: Kew accepts H. nana and recognizes subspecies; field account may reflect southwestern populations, not all Texas plants. Do not equate subspecies nana and californica measurements.

records.habit: Woody, much branched spreading–upright shrub commonly 1–3 m, sometimes forming thickets
records.leaves: Opposite simple ovate leaves, truncate base, coarse/blunt teeth; rough and aromatic foliage, frequently prickly stems
records.flowers: Stalked flattened flowerheads with narrow-tubed four-lobed corollas of several colors, including yellow, orange, pink, white and red
records.fruit: Rounded fleshy two-seeded drupes maturing dark purple to black
records.habitat: Non-native ornamental escape associated with disturbed habitats and edges
records.phenology: Flowering season varies by climate; Florida source records May–Dec in northern/central Florida and nearly year-round in south
records.taxon_note: Kew accepts hybrid Lantana × strigocamara; University of Florida uses L. strigocamara without hybrid sign. The native TX L. urticoides and historical L. camara are not to be substituted.

records.habit: Slender glabrous to minutely hairy annual/biennial herb to 70 cm (historical genus treatment)
records.leaves: Alternate or subopposite, nearly sessile, linear and entire
records.flowers: Pale lavender-blue two-lipped corolla with whitish palate, including slender curved basal spur 14–22 mm long; spur 6–11 mm, lower lip 6–11 mm
records.fruit: Capsules 2.5–3.5 mm; seeds densely tuberculate without longitudinal ridges (compare N. canadensis)
records.habitat: Sandy open woods, old fields and roadsides
records.taxon_note: 1999 flora uses Nuttallanthus texanus and directly cites Linaria texana. Kew POWO currently treats Linaria texana as accepted, whereas USDA GRIN and ITIS accept Nuttallanthus texanus. Preserve authority conflict; repository inventory Linaria texana is not an unrecognized taxon.

Kew and ITIS recognize this species; ITIS identifies synonym S. havardii. No sufficiently detailed individual species morphology directly validated in available sources; hold rather than importing another Seymeria species' characters.

Current plant description only validated to ssp. racemosa, source morphometric treatment needed
Subspecies-level Texas applicability of southwestern description unverified

source_policy: Direct historical flora treatment when available, alternative named botanical sources otherwise, no invented values
